claims.text: The diversity of phases in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during cooling and thermal exposure is driven by aluminum-mediated chemical short-range ordering.
During cooling from the high-temperature BCC state, Al atoms preferentially segregate.
Segregated Al forms chemically ordered nanoscale clusters.
Al-rich ordered clusters serve as nucleation sites for secondary phases such as B2 or sigma.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins as a high-temperature single-phase BCC alloy.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic mobility for Al segregation and local ordering.
The ordered Al-rich clusters reduce local free energy.
The ordered clusters trigger nucleation of ordered intermetallic phases.
Rapid quenching traps the high-temperature BCC arrangement.
Rapid quenching minimizes Al segregation and subsequent phase transformations.
Slowly cooled and isothermally held samples will contain more ordered precipitates than rapidly quenched samples.
The ordered precipitates formed after slow cooling and holding may include B2, sigma, or related phases.
Slowly cooled and held samples will show greater Al partitioning than rapidly quenched samples.
Rapidly quenched samples will largely retain the high-temperature BCC structure with little or no observable Al-driven ordering or secondary-phase formation.
The proposed mechanism operates at 600–800 degrees Celsius because diffusional kinetics are active in that range.
High applied stress or a reactive atmosphere may allow mechanisms other than Al-mediated ordering to dominate.
